column7: 2026-11-06: Decision (user's): in Scheduler.run_pending, when a job raises, keep running the other due jobs, then re-raise the FIRST exception once all have run. Reason: their supervisor restarts the worker and pages someone on crash, so errors must not be logged-and-swallowed. Not built yet; user will implement next session. Open point (mine, not decided): Job.run raises before last_run/_schedule_next_run, so the failed job stays due and retries every tick; decide whether to reschedule it (e.g. try/finally) as part of this change. Python versions older than 3.11 are supported, so don't rely on ExceptionGroup. Also done earlier this session: run_all(delay_seconds) now sleeps only between jobs.

2026-11-06: Built run_pending: runs all due jobs, logs each failure, re-raises FIRST exception after (no ExceptionGroup, py<3.11). My choice (open point settled): Job.run now reschedules in try/finally so a failing job isn't retried every tick. Test: FailingJobTest in test_schedule.py.
